Profits:

Strange how the “meme class” generates more threat than a thunderfury warrior

My assessment after playing classic:

  1. It’s a trade off compared to a geared fprot warrior. We likely edge out a threat oriented fprot warrior on thiccness while doing comparable threat. I think warriors actually have a higher threat potential, but bears are kind of a nice compromise.

  2. Our greatest weakness is early threat since maul, even with MCP is on next swing, and we lack any weapon skill. There’s a higher likelihood that we’ll be parried at the start.

  3. We definitely beat warriors on mobility and we’re great on fights like ouro since we can just feral charge back in.

  4. I think bears are serviceable MT’s. I think we’re excellent OT’s since we can generate much more threat with less rage.

  5. TBC is coming, and I’ll see you guys in Sunwell. However, I won’t be like some of the classic people and I won’t dump on the poor prot warriors when that time comes. lol

in the ultra min max of play. kiss goes to main tank for threat cap. then all the best warriors, then all the best rogues. and its strictly due to swing timer mechanics. 1, warriors are higher, and 2, their melee atks + heroic strikes + cleaves make up a larger portion of their damage than a rogues white hits do therefore they benefit more from kiss than a rogue does.

however bears are the sleeper class where nearly all of their damage is front loaded to maul so nearly 100% of their 450 dps vs a warriors 900 dps is actually a tie in effective use of the trinket. now of course both a warrior and a druid can pump harder than those two numbers. and a warrior can choose to pop rek and other CDs in combination with the trinket, however thats just cherry picking at that point. you have to calculate the portion of damage thats actually being increased by kiss, so crit executes to inflate dps would be overlooked by most when only 40% of their 1300 dps is auto attack related which would be the portion of their dps increased by kiss.

so again, look at the individual and calculate from there.
